divergences.old: Reading --collection, --project and --repo context from the first git remote on the connection's host in `git remote -v` order, which is sorted by remote name
divergences.toil: origin is offered first, then the other remotes in that order, and the first on the connection's host wins. The two differ only when origin and a remote whose name sorts before it (mirror, fork) are both on the host
divergences.why: origin is the clone's own remote, so it's the least surprising one to act on when two remotes point at the same server.

divergences.old: ado work-item schema --example-only printing the bare example with no envelope
divergences.toil: The flag stays; the example comes back as data in the usual envelope, so with the flag data is the example itself, not { schema, example }. Save .data to use it as an --input-file
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope, so an agent never has to guess which shape stdout holds. The allowed fields are excused only for calls with --example-only (`when`), so plain ado work-item schema must still return both.

divergences.old: ado work-item download fetching the attachment's relation URL, with the PAT, from whatever host the work item names (#69 item 1)
divergences.toil: The PAT goes only to baseUrl's origin: a relation URL on another host has its path and query re-pointed at baseUrl, with an ADO_ATTACHMENT_HOST warning
divergences.why: A server-supplied URL must not carry the user's credential to a host they didn't configure. A change a principle requires, so the integration makes it before a live run (CLAUDE.md, The command contract).

divergences.old: ado work-item download writing under --dir (by default a dot-folder in the working directory) anywhere on disk, replacing a file already there, and reporting saved with the platform's separator
divergences.toil: --dir defaults to .toil; the file is written inside the workspace, an existing file is refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the path, and saved uses forward slashes on every platform
divergences.why: A read-only command, whose file name comes from whoever uploaded the attachment, must not change files already on disk or write outside the workspace; paths in JSON output are the same on every platform.

divergences.old: ado work-item download reporting saved as --dir joined with the file name, so a relative --dir gives a relative path
divergences.toil: saved is always the absolute path written, with forward slashes, even when --dir is relative. The file lands in the same place (#233)
divergences.why: A relative --dir resolves against the workspace, which over MCP is not the caller's working directory, so a relative saved would point somewhere else. The absolute path says exactly where the file is.

divergences.old: ado project list, pipeline list, run list (with no --top), pr builds and pr list paging for as long as the server keeps answering
divergences.toil: The same stops (no continuation header, or a short $top/$skip page), plus a bound: after 1,000 pages the command fails with HTTP, naming the list, and a fix to narrow the request
divergences.why: A server that hands back a token or ignores $skip would otherwise be asked forever; the bound turns a hang into an error that says what happened.

divergences.old: ado project list, pipeline list, run list, pr list, pr builds and run logs --log-id surfacing a network failure or timeout as Node's bare fetch error, and reading only message from an error body (#69 item 4)
divergences.toil: The same requests, still with no 429 retry; a failure is core's NETWORK, TIMEOUT, AUTH, NOT_FOUND or HTTP error with the server's message and a fix, as every other ado command's is
divergences.why: Errors say plainly what went wrong and what to do next; a bare "fetch failed" says neither.

divergences.old: ado pr delete-comment available to every caller
divergences.toil: The same command on the CLI; toil mcp never serves it
divergences.why: Deletes are never exposed through MCP (CLAUDE.md, Writes).

divergences.old: ado work-item fields --save and work-item types --save writing fieldAliases, discoveredFields and discoveredTypes into the global config file
divergences.toil: There is no --save: passing it is the usual unknown-option INVALID_INPUT. Every call without it returns the data the contract records. A custom alias is fieldAliases on the connection
divergences.why: The saved fieldAliases were the built-in aliases filtered to fields the server has, and they were merged over those same built-ins when used, so saving never changed what a field name resolved to; nothing ever read discoveredFields or discoveredTypes. Removed on the maintainer's instruction of 2026-10-17 (KF6, #68), so no area command needs to write config.

divergences.old: ado work-item create and work-item update printing input-file keys overridden by flags to stderr and in meta.overrides, and work-item create --parent printing a failed link to stderr
divergences.toil: The same text as ADO_INPUT_OVERRIDDEN and ADO_PARENT_LINK_FAILED entries in meta.warnings; data and the exit code are unchanged
divergences.why: An MCP client never sees stderr, so a warning it can't see would fail silently. meta.warnings is the envelope's place for it (Output Contract).

divergences.old: ado pipeline run --wait giving up with "Timed out waiting for completion after <n>s" as a generic failure
divergences.toil: The same message as a TIMEOUT error, with a fix naming the build id to check
divergences.why: A wait that gives up is a timeout, and the fix says the build may still finish.

divergences.old: ado pipeline run --wait waiting as long as --timeout allowed
divergences.toil: The command's time limit is 11 minutes: the default 600 s wait plus a minute of polling. A longer --timeout ends in TIMEOUT at that limit unless TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS raises it
divergences.why: Every command has a time limit and can be cancelled; one that waits on slow work declares a longer limit, not none.

divergences.old: A missing collection or project telling the user to run config init
divergences.toil: "Could not determine Azure DevOps collection. Pass --collection, or set collection on the connection." (and the same for project), with a fix naming defaults.ado and the env var
divergences.why: toil has no config init yet; the error names what does exist.

divergences.old: ado work-item attach typing its data as an attachment with a name
divergences.toil: data is the server's answer passed through unchanged, as the contract specifies. The upload endpoint answers with an AttachmentReference, { id, url }, so the typed field the contract records never exists at run time
divergences.why: Nothing changes; the recorded field comes from a declared type, not from what the server returns, and a fixture shaped like the documented API can't carry it.

divergences.old: ado work-item fields --type typing each field with a type
divergences.toil: Unchanged: the type-scoped endpoint returns no type or readOnly, so both come out undefined and leave the JSON, as the contract records (#69 item 18, pinned)
divergences.why: A suspected bug is kept until a live run confirms it (CLAUDE.md, The command contract); the field is excused only for calls with --type.

divergences.old: ado run logs with no run id answering --build-id is required (from run, as pipeline logs)
divergences.toil: The id is a required positional, so a missing one is refused before the command runs: on the CLI as Missing required argument id, over MCP as the schema error naming id. Only an explicit empty id reaches the command, which says the run <id> is required
divergences.why: The reshape makes the run id the command's one positional; a required positional is checked by the parser, so the recorded message for a missing id has nowhere to come from

divergences.old: work-item link put --target into the relation URL as typed, and ids read with parseInt or taken from a response (build, iteration) into request paths unencoded; collection, project and repo were already encoded
divergences.toil: Every id is encoded as one path segment, --target included, so an id with path syntax in it stays one name; a value that would still name a . or .. segment is refused as INVALID_INPUT. Collection, project and repo are encoded, never refused, since Azure DevOps names may hold spaces and % (and the API accepts names the UI forbids)
divergences.why: An id names one resource, and the relation URL is stored by the server and read back as a path.

divergences.old: ado work-item download saving the attachment under the name the server gave it, once reduced to its last path segment
divergences.toil: A name Windows reserves for a device (CON, NUL, COM1 and the like, with any extension) is saved with a leading _, a : and everything after it is dropped, as are trailing dots and spaces, and the characters Windows forbids become _. filename in data is still the server's name; saved is where the file went. A --dir that names any of those is refused with INVALID_INPUT.
divergences.why: Windows reads each of those as a different file from the one named: a device, a stream inside an existing file, or the same name without its dots. The no-overwrite check has to see the file a write really lands on, and a name must work the same way on every platform.

divergences.old: ado pr list spelling the flags --creator <alias> and --reviewer <alias>
divergences.toil: The flags are --creator <id> and --reviewer <id>, and their help says the value is an identity id (a GUID, from ado whoami). Server sends it as the identity id filter, exactly as recorded; the value was never resolved from an alias
divergences.why: Azure DevOps Server and Azure DevOps Services are one area now (#495), so one idea has one flag. The recorded placeholder named a kind of value the command never looked up, and Services takes the identity id the same way.
